record.paper_title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems
record.original_question: Can one find a feasible description of the multiparametric family of continuous critical measures in the relevant class?

evidence.quote: (ii) to find a feasible description of the multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures in the given class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote a fixed class of finite positive Borel measures with compact support in the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ (for instance, measures whose support is contained in a prescribed system of analytic arcs, possibly with prescribed total masses on each connected component). For a measure $\mu$ in $\mathcal{A}$, define its logarithmic energy with external field $\varphi$ (a fixed real-analytic function on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\mu$) by
$$ E_\varphi(\mu) = \iint \log\frac{1}{|z-t|}\,d\mu(z)\,d\mu(t) + 2\int \varphi(z)\,d\mu(z). $$
Following the standard notion, call $\mu \in \mathcal{A}$ a continuous critical measure (with respect to $\varphi$ and the class $\mathcal{A}$) if for every smooth compactly supported vector field $h:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ that preserves the class $\mathcal{A}$ (i.e. the push-forwards $(\mathrm{id}+\varepsilon h)_*\mu$ lie in $\mathcal{A}$ to first order in $\varepsilon$), the first variation
$$ \left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{\varepsilon=0} E_\varphi\bigl((\mathrm{id}+\varepsilon h)_*\mu\bigr) = 0. $$
Equivalently (under mild regularity), $\mu$ is a continuous critical measure if the function
$$ R(z) := \left(\int \frac{d\mu(t)}{z-t} + \varphi'(z)\right)^2 $$
extends as a single-valued analytic function on $\mathbb{C}$ minus a finite set.

The collection of all such continuous critical measures in $\mathcal{A}$ (for a fixed $\varphi$) forms a multi-parameter family, parametrized by the periods of the associated quadratic differential $R(z)\,dz^2$ on the relevant Riemann surface.

Problem: Provide a feasible (explicit and effective) description of this multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures — for example, a parametrization of the family by an explicit set of moduli (such as a complete set of period or homological parameters of $R(z)\,dz^2$) together with effective conditions characterizing which parameter values correspond to genuine positive measures in $\mathcal{A}$.
artifact.category_tag: Critical measures and logarithmic potential theory
artifact.status_search_result: Critical measures and their connection with quadratic differentials have been developed substantially since 2006 (work of Martínez-Finkelshtein, Rakhmanov, and collaborators, e.g. the 2009 paper on critical measures and Stieltjes polynomials, and subsequent work on electrostatic partners through 2022). These works give structural results (representation by quadratic differentials, period parametrizations in specific genera) but no general feasible description of the full multi-parametric family has been provided; the problem appears to remain open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Critical measures, quadratic differentials, and weak limits of zeros of Stieltjes polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Critical measures are saddle points of the weighted logarithmic energy; their supports are unions of trajectories of a quadratic differential.
status_evidence.claim: Structural results parametrize critical measures via quadratic differentials, but general explicit descriptions remain incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic partners and zeros of orthogonal and multiple orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs second-order ODEs and electrostatic models for zeros via the electrostatic partner polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2022) work continues to address electrostatic models, indicating the general description problem is still actively being studied.
